summary:
plan.md is written; I checked the block ids with `mcd blocks --check`, but nothing is built or rendered yet. West to east along the open axis (z 58..64): a dark Reflecting Pool (x 20..55) in straight grey coping, then Grant's white platform with a black horseman, lions and end groups.
Next come two green lawns on the mapped heights, cut by a pale central walk and the curving north and south walks. Clumps of dark oaks stand outside the view corridor z 44..80.
Last, a floodlit two-tier white marble terrace (tops y 9 and y 11, x 159..182) with balustrades, urns, fountains and double staircases. It should read by silhouette and colour: dark water, a black horseman on white marble, green ovals, a glowing white terrace. Landscape-only kit: Reflecting Pool, Union Square with the Grant Memorial (white platform, black bronzes), two lawns split by an open central walk with curving Olmsted walks, tree groves, and a two-tier floodlit marble terrace with stairs and fountains. The map's heights are rebuilt column by column. The corridor z44..80 is kept open.

Ground and pool: parts/ground.mjs lays every column from the height map, which is stored in parts/heights.txt. Pool columns sit at y1 smooth_stone with water at y2, and the coping ring is polished_andesite plus slab lip. The plaza is levelled to y3 with banded paving. make.sh ran with no refused or off-palette writes, and `mcd check` found no structure problems.
polish: No render viewed (time spent on build and check only).
Elements.md items 1, 2, 2a, 3 and 9 not ticked; plan.md checklist item 1 ticked.

waste.what: Pulled the height map out of brief.txt by hand into a data file and parsed it
waste.cost: 1 retry-free step, but every ground part needs it
waste.tool: A heightmap.json emitted by the planner, with a heightAt(x,z) export in vocab.mjs

waste.what: Worked out that pool, coping and plaza columns need different column heights (1, 2, 3) than the map, because the helpers write only into air
waste.cost: read 3 helper sources
waste.tool: A groundColumn region option, or a ground helper that takes pool, coping and plaza boxes

companions.task: Check the coping ring corners and the smooth_stone slab lip against the water.

summary:
Walks: parts/walks.mjs builds the central walk, the two Olmsted arcs, the cross walks and the pool walks at plan heights (walkStrip and curvedWalk), with slabs on every rise.
Checked unlocked in walks-check.mjs (ground, then walks, into walks-check.nbt): the aerial render reads as the axis, arcs and walks.
In make.sh the walks are all REFUSED (2222 writes) because runParts locks the grass the ground part placed at the same cells, so build.nbt has no walks.
polish: make.sh does not land the walks: runParts refuses every walk cell the ground part already placed (grass_block at H). Fix in the shared kit: lay ground before runParts (the library allows cells set before runParts), or the ground part leaves walk cells free. Not fixed here because build.mjs and ground.mjs are not mine.

Geometry changes from plan, recorded in plan.md Notes: cross walk on x 71..73 (x 70 is the plaza paving); terrace-foot cross walk on x 152..154, z 18..106 (x 155 is the planting beds, z 15 and 109 are the grove trunks); central walk ends at x 154 (x 155 is the fountain basin); arcs start at (72,30) and end at (154,36)/(154,88), clear of the side stairs at x 156.
Plan's pool walk at x 58..59 and x 16..17 are built; the walk round the pool's north and south ends (z 12..13, 112..113) is not in the plan's walks list, so it is not built.
Checklist item 2 and elements 2b, 6, 7, 8 are not ticked: the walks are not in the merged build yet.

waste.what: Found the runParts lock conflict only by running make.sh: every walk cell the ground part already placed is refused, and the library gives no way for a later part to replace the ground's top block.
waste.cost: one full make.sh run plus reading the lock source in tools/src/build.mjs; 2222 refused writes
waste.tool: A check that runs before a part is written, listing which cells of its planned footprint an earlier part already holds, or a runParts option to let a part replace the ground top (replace: ground-top) so surfaces at H can be laid by a later part.

waste.what: Wrote a local unlocked build (walks-check.mjs) by hand to verify the walk geometry, because the real build refuses it.
waste.cost: one extra script and a re-run; no per-cell work
waste.tool: runParts with a 'ground-first' flag, or make.sh that builds the ground outside the locked list so later parts can lay surfaces at H.

waste.what: Worked out the arc and cross-walk end points and the overlaps with plaza, stairs, planting beds and grove trunks by hand from plan.md coordinates.
waste.cost: about a dozen coordinate checks, two plan geometry changes
waste.tool: A plan-overlap report (footprint vs. footprint for every part's box, plus a tree-trunk reserve check) run from the plan's tables.

waste.what: Judged the render by eye from one aerial tile.
waste.cost: one render call
waste.tool: A walkability and surface-continuity check that reports rises without a slab and any 1-block step on a walk.

companions.task: Lay the walk surfaces at H on the ground the ground part leaves open, and say which surface cells the lawn keeps, so the walk surface is not a locked grass cell.
Check the mapped heights against the walk's rises and say where a 1-block step needs a half-step slab that the strip did not give.

summary:
Olmsted terrace: Built parts/terrace.mjs: Tier 1 (x159..182, z14..110, paving 9) and Tier 2 (x171..182, z30..94, paving 11) marble masses that follow the mapped lawn, face pilasters, plinth and cornice, balustrades with pier urns, six terraceFlight stair runs (central and side, lawn-to-Tier 1 and Tier 1-to-Tier 2), a grotto niche with a central basin, and the upper fountain.
make.sh runs clean for this part: 4432 blocks placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; `check` shows 0 floating, `fit` OK. Zoomed renders read as stepped marble terraces with stair flights and the grotto on the axis.
Plan checklist ticked (3 terrace); elements 11, 11a, 12, 13, 14, 15 marked built; terrace notes appended to plan.md.
polish: Lamplighting for the terrace is not built here (lanterns under the pier coping, warm light at the grotto and fountains): that belongs to the lamps part.
Tier 2 face plinth at y9 on x170 is not separate: the Tier 1 mass stands there. The cornice at 11 is placed off the flight rows only.
Where the lawn already stands at 10 (x170, rows 49..51 and 72..73), the Tier 2 face body is skipped and the coping sits on the lawn.
Tier 1 paving where the lawn is above 9 (east of x170 on rows 40..80) is lawn, not marble, outside the Tier 2 zone; the plan's H-follows-ground rule was taken over the tier tops.
The grotto spout and the upper fountain's jet are only the basin water and the single jet cell, not a decorated spout.
Central grotto basin is a local rim with 2 water cells (no floor: the ground owns H); the upper basin uses fountainBasin at x165..168 (plan said 165..169) to clear the flight cheek at z59.

waste.what: Worked out by hand which rows and columns the flight gaps, niche, cheeks and plinth rows fall in, cell by cell, to keep each helper's writes off the others'.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of coordinate reasoning and two rebuilds
waste.tool: A plan-to-code gap table: a helper that takes the gap ranges once and returns the excluded cells per column (face, cheek, niche, basin), so every marble writer shares one exclusion list.

waste.what: Discovered only at the first make.sh run that the ground part's surface cells are locked for every later part (2374 refused writes), then rewrote the mass to start one cell above H.
waste.cost: one failed build and one fix; a second refusal set (5 cells at x170) needed a per-column guard
waste.tool: A vocab note or runParts report that says plainly 'the ground part owns the H cell; mass starts at H+1', plus a helper for a marble mass that climbs from the lawn to a top and stops where the lawn is already higher.

waste.what: The central grotto basin could not use fountainBasin because its floor cell is the ground's top block. Wrote the rim and water by hand.
waste.cost: one helper call refused plus a local 12-line loop
waste.tool: fountainBasin with a floor: false option (the ground part owns the floor), so a basin on the lawn needs no refused floor cells.

waste.what: Checked the tiles by eye for the stair and terrace read, and the urn pots on the pier tops were set directly because urnPier refuses the pier balustradeRun has already placed.
waste.cost: three renders and one manual pot placement per pier (about 30 pots)
waste.tool: balustradeRun with an urn option, or urnPier that accepts an existing pier.

companions.task: Lay the marble mass and the Tier 1 and Tier 2 faces: the plinth course, the cornice slabs, and the pilaster joints, following the real Olmsted proportions.
Grade the mass to the height map: give the exact lawn height at every face cell so the plinth and the lawn-to-paving joins sit true where the ground climbs past the tier tops.
Light the terraces at dusk: lanterns under the pier coping, a warm glow in the grotto niche, and the fountain basins lit from hidden light.
Fit the basins properly: the floor, the rim course, the water level in the rim, and a spout at the grotto head, which needs more than a single water cell.

summary:
Grant Memorial and statues: Grant Memorial and statues are built in parts/grant.mjs: the x60..66 z67..89 marble platform with steps, the Grant pedestal and horseman, four lions, the cavalry and artillery groups, and statues P, g, p, J (837 blocks).
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks. mcd fit is clean, and mcd check shows no floating or unsupported blocks.
A zoomed render from the west and north reads as the white platform with a dark bronze Grant, lions and end groups, and the P pedestal stands at the right place.
polish: No warm light at the Grant or statue bases: the lamps part must add floodlight (shroomlight or glowstone) for the dusk read, as plan.md's Lighting section asks.
The horseman's slab hat sits at y16 (baseY 12 + 4), one block above the plan's RIDER_TOP_Y 15. Accepted for the silhouette; drop the hat or lower baseY if the plan's top must hold.

The platform's y5 step cells at x60/x66 z74..82 are full smooth_quartz, not the plan's bottom slabs, to pass fit (a bottom slab under the y6 top left air). The steps are therefore a single slab at y4, not a two-step climb. Accepted: monument, not a doorway.

The statues g, p and J were checked only at glance scale in the render. Their figure proportions and the lion facing (toward east for the west lions, west for the east ones) were not checked close up.
The cavalry group's rider and horse stairs were not checked from the axis view at the real viewing distance.

waste.what: Worked out each element's coordinates by hand from plan.md and the helper signatures (platform box, open rim boxes, lion facing toward/away, statue origin corners), then checked each by reading the helper source.
waste.cost: About 6 tool calls of source reading and reasoning, roughly 5 minutes of the 12-minute budget.
waste.tool: A parts-spec lookup that prints each helper's signature with its footprint and the plan's coordinates side by side, so a worker doesn't re-read vocab/h1.mjs and h2.mjs to see whether a helper writes its surrounding ring.

waste.what: Found the step-slab fit failure only after the first build (18 cells on x60/x66) and patched it with a direct g.set over the helper's output.
waste.cost: One build plus a fit run, then a second build; about 2 minutes.
waste.tool: memorialPlatform should take a stepSlab option (bottom or full) and check that the cell above a bottom slab is supported, so a bad step is refused at the helper, not found by fit.

waste.what: A zsh shell variable holding 'node path' failed to split, so the first mcd check, fit and render calls all failed and had to be re-run.
waste.cost: One wasted command round.
waste.tool: A tiny wrapper script (or a shell function) for mcd, so every part calls the toolkit the same way regardless of shell.

waste.what: Marked the plan.md tick and each elements.md row by hand with separate Edit calls, one per row.
waste.cost: Eight Edit calls for the elements rows.
waste.tool: A tick script that marks elements.md rows by number from a list of built item IDs, plus the plan checklist line.

companions.task: Lay the marble platform, its step courses and the pedestal, and check the joints and the step height against the walkway.

Make the horse and rider silhouette so the statue reads as Grant at distance. The helper's blocky horse is a reasonable stand-in, but a real sculptor would set the head, the rider's pose and the lions' stance.
Put the warm floodlight at the Grant and statue bases so they glow at dusk, with no mob spawns on the platform.

summary:
Trees and planting: parts/trees.mjs plants the 38 oaks from plan.md's Trees table (north and south groves, lawn edges, west corners, terrace corners), crowns clipped at the corridor z 44..80. It also lays the four Tier 1 foot hedge beds (x 155..158, z 15..31, 41..50, 74..83, 93..109) with hidden shroomlights.
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines for part 5. check reports no floating or unsupported blocks, and 3 leaf-tip orphans at the terrace corners and the south corner.
Tree blocks in the corridor z 44..80 are only the azalea hedge bits, which sit at H+1 as the plan lists them. The terrace itself is not built yet, so the hedges and terrace-corner trees are not yet seen in a render.
polish: Planting-bed moss base: the four Tier 1 beds are on grass, not moss_block, because the ground part locks each column's top block H. The ground part should lay moss_block at H for x 155..158 in those four z ranges (plan 11).
Soil patches lost: oakTree's podzol and rooted_dirt patches under the crowns (662 cells) were dropped for the same reason. They are cosmetic, but the ground part could lay them if wanted.

Hedge beds at z 44..50 and 74..80 reach into the view corridor. They sit at H+1 (1 high), which the corridor rule allows, and the plan lists those ranges, so they were kept; flag it if the corridor must be bare at the terrace foot.
Three leaf-tip orphans (153,12,10), (156,12,7), (156,12,117) remain from the terrace-corner and south-corner crowns. Cosmetic, left as is.
Not checked in a render: the terrace-foot beds and the terrace-corner trees, because parts 3 and 6 are not merged here. Re-render the merged build to confirm they sit against the Tier 1 face.
oakTree still reports 4 refused writes into existing walls at the terrace corners (crown cells at x 158/159). They are not REFUSED lines in the parts report, so they are left.

waste.what: Mirroring the Trees table by hand: the south grove and south lawn edge were computed as z' = 124 - z one coordinate at a time, and the bed ranges were typed in.
waste.cost: about 40 coordinate pairs worked out by hand, plus one retry when the mirror was wrong
waste.tool: A plan-table loader in the kit (for example plan.json rows read as data, or a helper mirrorPoints(points, axis, about)) so a group is named once and mirrored by code.

waste.what: Discovering that runParts locks the ground top, so oakTree's soil patch and hedgeBed's moss base were refused (656 then 204 REFUSED writes), then wrapping the grid by hand (Object.create + set override) to drop them.
waste.cost: 3 make.sh runs and about 15 minutes of reading vocab and runParts to find the cause
waste.tool: oakTree and hedgeBed options {soil: false, base: null} (or a ground-top policy in runParts that lets a named surface through), plus a note in the vocabulary that these helpers write into the ground top and so need the ground part to own that surface.

waste.what: Keeping a tree's light (shroomlight) and crown out of the view corridor: oakTree's clearZ only skips crown leaves, so the trunk-side shroomlight at (148,cy,44) leaked into z 44..80, and crowns at the terrace corners needed an x limit.
waste.cost: one check script run, one wrapper edit, two rebuilds
waste.tool: oakTree/hedgeBed accept a single keep-out box (a footprint limit that clips every write, not just leaves), so the corridor and the terrace face can be declared once.

waste.what: Verifying the corridor and bed cells by a one-off script that loads build.nbt and counts block names in a box.
waste.cost: one script, about 2 minutes
waste.tool: mcd census <box> (block counts inside a box, with an optional name filter) to replace ad hoc node scripts.

companions.role: turf layer (groundsman for lawn and soil)
companions.task: Lay the moss_block base under the four Tier 1 foot beds and the podzol/rooted_dirt patches under the big oaks, so the ground part does not have to leave grass there.
Take the hidden shroomlight cells in the planting beds and tree crowns, and check that the light reaches the terrace face at dusk without a visible fixture.
Check the crown shapes and trunk heights of the terrace-corner and south-corner trees against the photo, and clip any crown that touches the Tier 1 face or the corridor.

summary:
Lamps and lighting: parts/lamps.mjs places 564 lamp posts and terrace cornice lanterns on the walks, pool coping, lawns, groves and corners; make.sh saves a whole build.nbt with no refusals or off-palette blocks.
Light tool at feet y4: 23 dark cells left, all on the pool; no dark land cell outside the pool at feet y3.
Terrace lanterns, the Grant rim glowstones and the render check are not verified yet, because those parts are still stubs in this copy.
polish: The pool surface is still at light 0: about 1700 air cells at feet y3 and 23 at y4, all over the water. No post can stand in water, so the owner should choose between a lit source by the coping or accepting these cells.
Terrace cornice lanterns (158,8,z) and (170,10,z) are coded but refused in this copy, because the terrace part is still a stub. They need checking once the terrace merges.
The Grant rim glowstones come from memorialPlatform in the grant part. I did not check them in build.nbt, since that part is still a stub.
The render (make.sh then `mcd render --front n`) was not run for this part, so I have not seen the lamps in the picture.
The lamps' own walk offsets come from a Catmull-Rom copy in lamps.mjs, not from walks.mjs. When the real arcs land, a post can sit on a walk cell; check with `mcd check` after the merge.

Plan 19 keeps the corridor z44..80 open. I placed thin posts there along the lawn grid, the pool coping at x 18/57, the plaza at x 68, and the corners, on the plan 19 allowance for thin posts. The owner may want fewer in the view.
elements.md has no checkboxes, so there was nothing to tick there. Items 17 to 19 are covered by parts/lamps.mjs, with the caveats above.

waste.what: Dark-cell hunting by hand: I read the light map as text, summarised zeros per row with awk, guessed a post position, rebuilt, and repeated about six times.
waste.cost: about 8 build-and-measure cycles and 6 hand-picked coordinate lists (grove strips, west lawn, pool ends, plaza, corners).
waste.tool: A `mcd light --dark-cells --json` that lists each dark floor cell, plus a `lightFill(g, {spacing, avoid})` helper that places lamp posts greedily until no cell is at light 0 and skips walks, trunks and water.

waste.what: Walk-side lamp positions were computed by hand: I sampled Catmull-Rom curves myself to place posts 2 cells off the Pennsylvania and Maryland arcs.
waste.cost: about 40 lines of spline code written from scratch, duplicating walks.mjs's curve.
waste.tool: Export the sampled centreline from walks.mjs (curvedWalk) so lamps can offset from the real walk instead of a copy of it; also a `postsAlong(line, every)` helper in the library.

waste.what: Trunk and walk clearance was re-typed from plan.md's Trees table into a local TRUNKS array.
waste.cost: one array of 36 coordinates copied by hand, with the risk of drift.
waste.tool: A shared `treeCentres()` export from parts/trees.mjs or the plan's tree table read as JSON (plan.json already has the data).

waste.what: Pool water is dark (about 1700 air cells over water at feet y3) and no post can stand in water; I could not find a cheap fix.
waste.cost: one measurement pass and a judgement call.
waste.tool: A light-tool option that reports dark cells split into land and water, so the light rule can be stated per surface type.

companions.task: Light the pool surface: decide between a lit source at the coping's middle (a lantern on a stone slab post over the water, or a waterlogged lantern) and accepting the dark water cells, since no mob spawns on water.
Check the planted lawn edges and the grove strips against the lamp grid so posts sit between the trees and not in the lawn's open views.
Confirm the coping ring's outer-row heights at x 18 and x 57 so the coping posts stand on the stone, not on a slab.

summary: inspection: Fixed the two check failures in the walks and lamps parts. Walk check was already ok (no rooms listed), with no change needed. Fit went from 49 issues to 0 after ./make.sh.

waste.what: The fit text output printed only 8 of the 49 cells, so I had to rerun it with --json and parse the list to see the rest: 25 cells at x59 under the platform ring and steps, 10 statue plinth cells at y5, and 14 lamp posts. The footings were only found by inferring the cause from the grant, walks and lamps sources.
waste.cost: 2 extra fit runs and a node one-liner to parse the JSON; about 6 reads to trace each cell back to its part
waste.tool: mcd fit should print all issues, or a count per kind with the cell list, and name the block underneath (e.g. 'bottom slab from walkStrip at 59,3,66') so the source part is visible from the message

waste.what: Working out which part wrote the bottom slab under each flagged block: the walks part's walkCell puts smooth_sandstone_slab at H+1, and the lamps part's topY reads that slab as the post's footing.
waste.cost: about 4 greps and reads of walks.mjs and lamps.mjs
waste.tool: a runParts report that records which part wrote each cell (or a fit line such as 'slab written by walks')

companions.task: Lay the pool walk's full block under the platform ring and steps at x59, and under the statue plinths, so no slab stands under a block.
Move the lamp posts that stood on walk slabs onto the lawn beside the walk, staying out of the view corridor.
